run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T18:51:38Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate warning on otel-demo/frontend-proxy is driven by frontend-proxy's own ingress error spans: the 5m ingress error-span rate read 0.0111 at 18:50:38, matching the alert's current value 0.0111, and peaked at 0.0185 around 18:54:38. The 503s are produced when frontend-proxy's upstream is the frontend service: frontend-proxy's access log records '503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' for requests routed to the frontend cluster, and the failing traces contain only load-generator and frontend-proxy spans (ingress 503 plus a 'router frontend egress' span with error=true and http.status_code=0), with no frontend server span, i.e. the frontend closed the connection before any response was started. The only frontend pod (frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t, the single endpoint of Service frontend) is Running and Ready with 0 restarts, steady memory ~123-129 MB of its 200Mi limit and no memory failure counter, while its CPU is CFS-throttled roughly 28-37% of periods; frontend-proxy itself is Ready with 0 restarts and only 5-8% throttling. Request rates were flat (frontend-proxy ingress ~9.9-10.6 spans/s, frontend spans 30-41/s with no gap) while the error rate swung between 0 and 0.0185, so a load surge or a throttling change does not explain the burst. The in-container reason the frontend aborts in-flight connections is not established: the frontend container produced no log lines at all in the windows queried and its span metrics carry STATUS_CODE_UNSET rather than recorded error status, so the evidence stops at the frontend pod. The fraud-detection container's OOMKill at 18:51:40 is a separate change in the window that is not tied to these 503s.

claims.text: The alert's current value 0.01111111111111111 matches the frontend-proxy ingress STATUS_CODE_ERROR span rate of 0.011111111111111112 sampled at 2026-11-16T18:50:38Z, the last 2-minute sample before the alert start (18:51:38Z); the same series peaked at 0.018518518518518517 at 18:54:38Z and returned to ~0.0037-0.0044 by 19:08:38Z.

frontend-proxy's access log shows the error responses are HTTP 503 with Envoy response flag UC and response-code detail 'upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}' toward the upstream cluster named 'frontend', e.g. at 2026-11-16T18:44:59.248Z for 'GET /api/products/9SIQT8TOJO' (800 ms) and at 18:44:59.281Z for 'GET /' (767 ms); the neighbouring successful request in the same sample was '200 - via_upstream'.

In the sampled frontend-proxy error traces (18:26:55-18:45:48), 8 frontend-proxy 'ingress' spans have error=true/http.status_code=503/otel.status_code=ERROR and each has a child 'router frontend egress' span with error=true and http.status_code=0; the corresponding traces contain no frontend server span at all (trace 006109e39dbc3e0e38ea35e8110e2b5c holds only the load-generator 'user_browse_product'/'GET' spans and the frontend-proxy 'ingress'/'router frontend egress' spans).

Over the whole authorized window (17:51:38-19:09:06) the only nonzero request-error span increases were frontend-proxy ingress 15.2 error spans, fraud-detection 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 5.07, recommendation '/flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 3.04 and ad 'flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream' 3.05; the STATUS_CODE_ERROR series returned for frontend (GET, POST, executing api route ... , grpc.oteldemo.*) and for checkout PaymentService/Charge, checkout CheckoutService/PlaceOrder, payment GET and accounting 'orders receive' were all 0, and no cart or product-catalog ERROR series was returned, so their error state is unknown.

The frontend upstream frontend-proxy resets against is the single pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t (Running, Ready, restartCount 0, no last-terminated state), which is the only address (100.96.4.88:8080) in the Service 'frontend' endpoints; it is owned by ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5, owned by Deployment 'frontend', and that ReplicaSet was created 2026-11-16T18:12:40Z with no older frontend ReplicaSet present.

The frontend container runs with limits cpu=100m/memory=200Mi (requests 50m/100Mi) and the frontend Deployment defines no liveness, readiness or startup probes; the Deployment reports replicas=1, ready=1, available=1, updated=1. frontend-proxy runs with limits cpu=30m/memory=50Mi, also without probes, replicas=1 and ready=1.

The frontend container was CPU-throttled in roughly 28-37% of CFS periods across 18:32-19:08 (0.281-0.369) and its working set grew monotonically from 122.8 MB to 128.5 MB, always below the 200Mi limit, with container_memory_failcnt 0 throughout; no OOM or restart occurred on this pod. The frontend-proxy container was throttled only 0.047-0.084 over the same period.

Traffic volume was flat while the error rate swung: the frontend-proxy ingress span rate stayed 9.86-10.62 spans/s from 18:32 to 19:08, and the frontend total span rate stayed 29.5-41.4 spans/s with no zero/gap sample between 18:29 and 19:00, so no restart or traffic surge of the frontend is visible in those series.

The failures are visible to the caller too: the matching load-generator request spans carry error=true, http.status_code=503, otel.status_code=ERROR (8 rows in the sampled error traces, e.g. operation 'GET' at 18:44:59.248Z with duration 802399 us).

A change did occur at the alert time on an unrelated pod: fraud-detection container in pod fraud-detection-9fb7d885b-xdwst has lastState terminated with reason OOMKilled, exitCode 137, finishedAt 2026-11-16T18:51:40Z, restartCount 1, and was running again from 18:51:40Z. Its container logs returned no lines in 18:40-18:53, so its own application reason is unknown.

Neither CPU throttling nor request volume follows the error pattern: frontend CFS throttling stayed in a narrow 0.281-0.369 band and frontend-proxy ingress held ~10 spans/s while the frontend-proxy ingress error rate moved between 0 and 0.0185 (nonzero from 18:29, elevated 18:46-18:56, again ~0.004 afterwards), and the frontend working set only grew slowly with failcnt 0, so a throttling step, a traffic surge or frontend memory exhaustion is not what separates the failing periods from the quiet ones.

A frontend crash/restart is not supported as the mechanism: the frontend container has restartCount 0 with no terminated state, its span rate shows no gap, and its memory series has no drop to a fresh-process level, so the connection terminations are not explained by the process being restarted.

The fraud-detection OOMKill (exitCode 137 at 18:51:40Z) as the cause of this alert was considered and rejected: frontend-proxy ingress errors were already elevated before that event (0.0111 at 18:46:38 and 0.0117 at 18:48:38) and nonzero from the start of the available series at 18:29, the 503s are upstream connection resets from the frontend cluster rather than failures of checkout/payment, and the whole-window error increases for checkout PlaceOrder, checkout PaymentService/Charge and payment GET were 0.

The mechanism of the alert is that the frontend pod's HTTP server aborts a small fraction of in-flight requests before sending response headers, which frontend-proxy reports as 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}; the in-process cause is not identified, and the sustained ~28-37% CFS throttling of the frontend at its 100m CPU limit is only a candidate contributor (throttling was flat across the error bursts, so it does not explain the 18:46-18:56 elevation by itself).

The flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream error spans seen for ad (3.05), recommendation (3.04) and fraud-detection (5.07) over the window are a separate candidate failure mode (gRPC streaming disconnects) and are not tied by any observed evidence to the frontend-proxy 503s; they remain an unrelated possible problem.

Obtain the frontend application's own logs or an in-process diagnostic for 18:40-19:00 to identify why it closes connections (the container currently yields no log lines), and inspect frontend-proxy's upstream connection/reset counters and retry policy; enabling retries on the frontend route would convert these single-connection resets into successful requests.

Review the RequestErrorRate rule's threshold/for-duration: a recurring low background of single-connection resets exists across the whole available series (nonzero at 18:29, 0.0037-0.0044 at the end of the window), so an alert that fires on any rate above zero will flap; a threshold above the observed background or a longer for-duration would reduce noise. Also consider raising the frontend CPU limit above 100m, since the pod is throttled ~30% of CFS periods.

gaps: The frontend container emitted no log lines in the queried windows (fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t returned 0 lines/0 bytes for 18:44:50-18:45:30 and 18:26:00-18:56:00), so the in-process reason the frontend closes connections could not be read and is unknown.

The RequestErrorRate alerting rule was not returned by list_prometheus_rules (no data for that rule name), so its exact expression, threshold and for-duration are unknown; only the span-metric error rate that matches the alert's current value is available.

Span-metric series begin around 18:28-18:29 and the returned Jaeger traces end at 18:45:48, so the 18:46-18:58 elevation that triggered the alert has no trace-level detail, and there is no pre-18:28 baseline.

Kubernetes events were only available for 18:49:37-19:01:37, and no change/deployment history integration (change_history) is available in this Run, so earlier events and any configuration changes cannot be checked.

Whether the connection terminations correspond to a particular frontend route or downstream dependency cannot be determined: the failing traces contain no frontend span and the failing ingress spans expose no path tag.
The flagd EventStream errors on ad, recommendation and fraud-detection were not investigated to their own root cause.
next_steps: Read the frontend container's stdout/stderr (or exec into frontend-675fd7b5c5-ssc7t) for 18:40-19:00 to identify why it aborts in-flight requests.
Check frontend-proxy's Envoy admin statistics for upstream_cx_reset/upstream_rq_retry and confirm the frontend route's timeout and retry policy.

If the intent is to alert on real user impact, raise the RequestErrorRate threshold above the observed background or lengthen its for-duration, and compare against an error-ratio metric rather than an absolute rate.

Treat the frontend CPU limit (100m, ~30% CFS throttling) as a capacity review item and the fraud-detection OOMKill (exit 137 at 18:51:40Z) as a separate follow-up, since neither is shown to cause these 503s.

A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.
